question: On the ewt360 account login page, submitting the login form sends a POST to the account-login API whose `password` field is an AES-encrypted token (e.g. the password 13819912565 is sent as A987B688ACCCDB600F78FE657DF98627). Locate the single complete login-path password encryption entry function that the submit handler calls to transform the request `password` field. Return exactly one JSON object (see answer_format). Do NOT return the login submit handler that calls it, the lower-level AES helper it delegates to, the generic CryptoJS AES primitive, or a byte-identical encryptor in another chunk that is not invoked on the login request. Only code under captures is in scope.

function_name.description: Identifier on the function as it appears in the captured bundle (the name after `function`, or the variable/property it is assigned to).

file.description: captures-relative path to the file containing the function; must match visible_corpus.

code.description: Exact text [start_offset,end_offset); one complete function (balanced braces).

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; no markdown fences unless the harness requires it.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function (balanced braces), not a fragment or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list.
Return the app-level password encryption entry function that is actually invoked on the login submit path, not a byte-identical duplicate in another (lazily-loaded) chunk.
Do not return the login submit handler, the lower-level AES helper, or the generic CryptoJS AES primitive.
anchor_definition_general: For this case, the anchor is the app-level password encryption entry function recorded by the metadata anchor in 1.json. It is the complete function directly reached from the login submit handler for the request `password` field, including any input guards and delegation used by that entry. A lower-level AES helper that the entry calls is a high-value helper, but it is not the top-1 metadata anchor. A function is generic when it is a reusable utility (hash/encode/encrypt/serialize/normalize/collect-features), a control-flow dispatcher, or a preparation routine whose body would look the same regardless of this behavior. The request-sending service that merely emits an already-built value is a wrapper rather than the anchor.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example (a different site, for illustration only): a login page sends POST /user/login whose `password` field is an AES ciphertext. On submit the chain is: read form values -> submit handler assigns request.password = passwordEntry(request.password) -> passwordEntry handles empty values and calls a site AES helper -> the helper binds key/iv and returns ciphertext -> the ajax service sends the body. If the metadata anchor is passwordEntry, return that complete entry function. The lower-level AES helper is close but below the anchor; the submit handler and ajax sender are wrappers; a duplicate encryptor in an unrelated chunk is off-chain.
